record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: In the limited fork-join model with n distributed queues and jobs that create only k much smaller than n tasks, how large can k grow while the queues still exhibit asymptotic independence as n tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: While good progress has been made on analyzing the limited fork-join model, open problems remain. It is unclear how much larger k can be made while still achieving asymptotic independence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the limited fork-join queueing model defined as follows. There are $n$ parallel server stations, each with its own FIFO queue and a single server with unit service rate (service times are i.i.d. from some distribution, e.g. exponential). Jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate $\Lambda(n)$. Upon arrival, each job splits into $k = k(n) \le n$ tasks, which are dispatched to $k$ distinct stations chosen uniformly at random; a job is considered complete only when all of its $k$ tasks have finished service. Assume the per-server load $\rho = \Lambda(n)\, k(n)/n$ is held in $(0,1)$.

We say the system exhibits asymptotic independence (in the regime $n \to \infty$) if, for any fixed integer $m$, the joint stationary distribution of the workloads at any $m$ of the $n$ queues converges to the product of $m$ copies of the stationary workload distribution of a single M/G/1 queue with load $\rho$. More generally, one may ask for joint independence of $k(n)$ queues (with $k(n)$ growing with $n$).

It is known that asymptotic independence of any $k(n)$ queues holds whenever $k(n) = o(n^{1/4})$.

Problem. Determine the largest growth rate of $k(n)$ (as a function of $n$) for which asymptotic independence of the queues continues to hold in this limited fork-join model. In particular, does asymptotic independence persist for $k(n)$ growing faster than $n^{1/4}$, and what is the sharp threshold?
artifact.status_search_result: Existing work establishes asymptotic independence of the queues in the limited fork-join model under the condition $k(n) = o(n^{1/4})$, generalizing earlier results that handled only a fixed number of queues. The sharp growth rate of $k(n)$ for which asymptotic independence persists has not been determined, and improving the $n^{1/4}$ threshold remains open.

status_evidence.title: Delay Asymptotics and Bounds for Multi-Task Parallel Jobs
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic independence of any k(n) queues is established under the condition k(n) = o(n^{1/4}), generalizing previous asymptotic independence results for a fixed number of queues.
status_evidence.claim: Best known sufficient condition for asymptotic independence in the limited fork-join model is k(n) = o(n^{1/4}).

status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic independence of any k(n) queues established when k(n) = o(n^{1/4}).
